text: Everything so far has generated numbers through a column — IDENTITY, tied permanently to one table. SEQUENCE objects break that assumption entirely: a standalone number generator you can use anywhere you want.

Create sequence dbo dot LessonSeq, start with 1, increment by 1. A sequence is its own database object — it isn't attached to any particular table or column. Start with 1 sets the first value it hands out; increment by 1 sets how much it goes up each time.

Select next value for dbo dot LessonSeq as NextID. Each call hands out the next number in the sequence — 1, then 2, then 3 — and that number is now used, never handed out again. You can call it on its own, or inline inside an insert.

Here's the real difference from IDENTITY: LessonOrders and LessonInvoices both default to next value for the same LessonSeq. The same sequence can be shared across multiple tables, if you want several tables drawing from one common pool of numbers — something an identity column locked to one table could never do.

Declare at NewOrderID int equals next value for dbo dot LessonSeq. This is the other real advantage: you can get a number before you've inserted anything at all — useful when you need that key value to build related rows first. With IDENTITY, you must insert first, then read the value back.
Next lesson: DEFAULT constraints — filling in a value automatically whenever a column is left out of an insert.
